build.note: Read from the sealed 1.4.3.5 raw capture with its own descriptors; no export, no new capture. The same assets were also decoded from the open 2.1.1.0 capture: 109 of the 110 header-bearing modifier files are byte-identical there, and the changed one (GRM_Recoil_Controller_03, operands 0.8836 to 0.95) keeps the same header values.

question: Which recoil and dispersion mechanics do the executable's readable strings and the tweakables registry state, beyond field names?

sourceFacts.method: The matching-strings list recorded on 7 October from bf6.exe (inspection.json, read-only PE inspection, no execution) was re-read for mechanic statements. The two tweakable rows it names were located in GRX_WeaponsAndGadgets of the sealed 1.4.3.5 capture by row name (Field_0c59fa06) and their boolean Field_42c8b257 re-read at the byte offset derived from the descriptor table (manifest-L4039.json, rawchecks-L4039.json).

control.description: Row names resolve to exactly one instance each (instances 5 and 6 of the registry file); the boolean read at the computed offset equals the decoded value.

points: GRX_WeaponsAndGadgets rows RecoilCompensationConsumesAimPitch (instance 5, Field_42c8b257 at file offset 552) and RecoilCompensationConsumesAimYaw (instance 6, offset 640) are both true. The executable carries the matching tweakable names TweakableRefType_GS_RecoilConsumesAimPitch and _Yaw. Reading: the player's counter-aim input is subtracted from the recoil state rather than only moving the camera, so compensation also reduces the later recovery, which depends on the remaining displacement. The site's recoil-control slider subtracts the expected kick from the delivered vector, which has the same effect on the state.

The executable holds the enumeration DispersionAsRecoil_Never, _Always, _OnlyWhenBenefittingFromBipod, _OnlyWhenMountedUp, _OnlyWhenMountedSide, _OnlyWhenSupported and the dispersion fields UseDispersionAsRecoilOnly and AddDispersionAsRecoilOnly (engine dump). Deployed and mounted fire can convert dispersion into recoil; the vocabulary (bipod, mounted up, mounted side) matches the three modifier conditions read in L4038. Which weapons or states select a value other than Never is not read: no GS dispersion field has been identified as the enumeration.

WeaponComponent_RecoilForceTicksBits names a replicated tick count for recoil force. A tick-quantized delivery is a concrete mechanism for a fixed post-shot pause before recovery, which the 14 October replay (Analyzer RECOIL_SPREAD_MODEL.md) found fits the September recordings at about 33 ms; this is a lead, not a decoded rule.

WeaponAttribute_RecoilSmoothness and WeaponAttribute_RecoilDecayMultiplier are the attribute names behind the two Smooth-recoil operands (RecoilDuration override, decay-factor multiply); WeaponAttribute_RecoilAmount, _RecoilVariation, _RecoilDirection, _ADSStationaryDispersion, _ADSDispersionIncrease, _ADSMoveDispersion and _HipFireDispersionIncrease name the other attribute channels.

GunSwayDispersionAction_{Default, Moving, Jumping, Sprinting} and GunSwayDispersionBehaviorAction_{Default, MovingJumpingSprinting} are the native movement-state enumerations behind the stationary and moving dispersion rows: Jumping is a separate angle action from Moving but shares the moving behavior.
TweakableRefType_KS_DisableSuppressionEffectOnGunsway and the GunSwaySuppression* members in the engine dump show a suppression penalty path on gun sway; no BF6 GS field has been tied to it.

inference: Names in the executable establish that the mechanism exists in the code; they do not give its arithmetic or which assets activate it.
unresolved: The field or enum that selects DispersionAsRecoil per weapon or state; the tick length behind RecoilForceTicksBits; whether the suppression gun-sway path is active in multiplayer.
siteImpact: None. Document the compensation reading beside the recoil-control slider; no numeric change.

referenceFiles.use: matchingStrings[3..77]: readable strings of bf6.exe (read-only inspection, 7 October)

leads.title: Recoil compensation consumes aim (two true tweakables), and the executable's dispersion-as-recoil, recoil-force-tick and attribute names
leads.summary: GRX_WeaponsAndGadgets rows RecoilCompensationConsumesAimPitch and Yaw are true (raw-checked), so counter-aim input is subtracted from recoil state; the executable names a DispersionAsRecoil enumeration (never, always, bipod, mounted up, mounted side), a replicated recoil-force tick count, the Smooth attribute names RecoilSmoothness and RecoilDecayMultiplier, and the movement-state dispersion actions.
leads.reopenWhen: A GS field or enum resolves DispersionAsRecoil per weapon, a readable implementation gives the tick length, or an in-game test shows compensation changing recovery.

assets.question: Are the recoil-compensation-consumes-aim rows true?
assets.conclusion: Both named rows exist as instances 5 and 6; Field_42c8b257 is true on each at the computed offsets.
